dedupe_keys.name: t garden real and synthetic quasi planar internet backbone topologies

description: T-Garden is a curated collection of physical-layer Internet backbone network topologies, both real ones gathered and cleaned from public sources and synthetic quasi-planar topologies generated to resemble them, released with a 2026 Scientific Data article by Tamás-Zsolt Képes, Noémi Gaskó, János Tapolcai and Balázs Vass. Each network is a graph of nodes with geographic positions and fibre links, curated so that links do not cross unrealistically, which matters for studies of geographically correlated failures. Coverage: backbone networks of many countries and regions worldwide plus synthetic sets; version 1 archived on 2 July 2026. Format and access: a ZIP archive of about 51 MB with GML files, plots and licence information on Zenodo, a snapshot of the public GitHub repository kepestamas/T-Garden-Networks; free under CC BY 4.0 for the project, with the SNDlib subset under the ZIB Academic License and the Interroute-Italy subset under the GPL, and citation of the article requested. Caveats: public backbone maps are incomplete and dated; synthetic networks are statistical look-alikes, not real systems. Simulation uses: network topology inputs for resilience and cascading failure studies of regional disasters, routing and capacity planning, and benchmarking of network design algorithms. Related records: SNDlib, the Internet Topology Zoo and TeleGeography submarine cable data give related topologies.
